# Trundle Manor

> Antique taxidermy, medical curiosities and kooky oddities in a private Pittsburgh home. Tours by arrangement. Rated 4.8 from 312 Google reviews.

- Type: Tourist Attraction
- Address: 7724 Juniata St, Pittsburgh, PA 15218, USA
- Phone: (412) 916-5544
- Email: mrarm@trundlemanor.com
- Website: https://ronaks-code.github.io/sitelift-demos/escape-rooms/pa/trundle-manor/
- Google Maps: https://maps.google.com/?cid=10488115032705989761&g_mp=Cidnb29nbGUubWFwcy5wbGFjZXMudjEuUGxhY2VzLlNlYXJjaFRleHQQAhgEIAA
- Google rating: 4.8 from 312 reviews


## About
Trundle Manor is a tourist trap based on the eternal need to show off the unusual. It's a private home on Juniata St in Pittsburgh, packed with taxidermy, medical curiosities, unusual artwork, strange inventions and historic artifacts.
Some pieces were collected, some handmade and some gifted to the owners, and each one has its own story. Velda von Minx leads the tours, and one reviewer said it felt more like visiting someone's fascinating home than touring a conventional museum.
Visitors have given Trundle Manor a 4.8 rating from 312 Google reviews.

## Services
- Tour: A walk through the house and its oddities with Mrs. Von Minx.
- Escape room and events: Beyond the tours, the Manor also hosts an escape room and events.

## FAQ
Q: What does a visit cost?
A: One reviewer said they ask for a $20 donation or a gift related to the theme.

Q: Can I just drop by?
A: This is a private home, so please arrange your visit in advance. Don't show up early, and get in touch if you can't make your scheduled time.

Q: Are there restrooms?
A: Restrooms are not available to the public, so please plan accordingly.

Q: Are tours ever paused?
A: Tours are suspended while the Manor is on its Halloween break, and contact forms and messages aren't answered during that time. You can still send a form for a future date and it will be answered after the break.

## What customers say
- "Trundle Manor was one of the most unique and unexpectedly charming places we visited during our trip. If you have an appreciation for the strange, unusual, and macabre, this place is absolutely worth experiencing.

At first glance, it's a collection of taxidermy, medical curiosities, unusual artwork, strange inventions, and just about every oddity imaginable. But spending some time here reveals something much more interesting. This isn't simply a museum of bizarre objects. It's a very personal collection that reflects the interests, creativity, and relationship of the couple who put it together.

Some items were collected, others handmade, and still others gifted to the owners. Everything seems to have its own story, and somehow it all feels perfectly at home together. I particularly enjoyed seeing the facial casts of classic horror legends Boris Karloff, Bela Lugosi, and Vincent Price.

We had the pleasure of meeting Velda, who was welcoming and made the experience feel more like visiting someone's fascinating home than touring a conventional museum.

What surprised me most was how warm and personable the place felt. Despite being surrounded by things commonly associated with death and the macabre, there was nothing particularly disturbing about the experience. Quite the opposite, actually. There's a tremendous amount of personality, affection, and creativity here.

Trundle Manor is a wonderful reminder that a collection can tell you as much about the people who assembled it as the objects themselves. We thoroughly enjoyed our visit and would gladly return. Just be sure to arrange your visit in advance!" (Jonathan Lamb, 5/5)
- "I’ve been wanting to see the collection at Trundle Manor for years….it met and possibly exceeded all of my expectations. If you love morbid curiosities, quirky taxidermy, and odd and unique stuff, you'll enjoy this place. My only complaint is that they need more merch….t-shirts, hats, coffee mugs….anything….everything! This is a private home where the couple who owns it are kind enough to share their collection with the general public, so they have a few basic rules to follow such as not showing up early and contacting them if you can’t make your scheduled time. The wife, Velda von Minx, gave us our tour and she has lots  of wonderful stories about the collection and their home and was kind enough to answer our many questions!" (Joseph Morgan, 5/5)
- "I'm so glad I stopped here with my family on our trip to Pittsburgh!  It's was amazing how much was able to fit in this house.  Mrs. Von Minx gave us an incredible tour and was so informative.  The family just enjoys showing off their amazing oddities for fun.  They ask for a $20 donation or a gift related to the theme, so I actually had fun trying to figure out a good gift for the house although $20 is really not much to ask for.  In my opinion, it was worth a lot more.  Be aware that restrooms are not available to the public, so please plan accordingly and have fun!  I can't wait to tell my friends and family to check it out" (Jamilyn Psaros, 5/5)
- "A unique hidden gem! Trundle Manor is a very interesting place to view taxidermy, medical oddities, and historic artifacts. Velda was our guide—incredibly knowledgeable and genuinely entertaining. A must-visit for anyone who loves the unusual!" (Dave Camus, 5/5)
- "If creepy was a person and house. Full of the most lovingly unhinged and grotesque things you can't look away from. The owner was so sweet, personable and happy to share. Halloween year round." (Josh Weber, 5/5)
